s: A company replicates about 150 TB of data each month from Amazon EC2 instances in us-east-1 to its on-premises data center over an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection that runs over the internet. Data transfer out charges have become significant. The company already has a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to the same Region for other workloads, and it has enough spare capacity. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective?
o: Route the replication traffic over the existing Direct Connect connection by using a private virtual interface, so that the data is billed at Direct Connect data transfer out rates.
Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration and stage the replicated data in Amazon S3 before the data center downloads it.
Order AWS Snowball Edge devices each month to ship the data to the data center.
Serve the replicated data through an Amazon CloudFront distribution that the data center downloads from.

w.y: Data transfer out over Direct Connect is billed at Direct Connect rates, which are much lower per GB than data transfer out to the internet (which is what a VPN over the internet pays), and data in over Direct Connect is free. With spare capacity on an existing connection, moving the traffic costs nothing extra (task 2.6: data transfer modeling).

o.A: Correct. Same data, lower per-GB rate, on a connection that is already paid for.
o.B: Transfer Acceleration is a premium for faster internet transfers into and out of S3. It adds cost and still uses internet data transfer.
o.C: Monthly devices add shipping and handling time. Snowball Edge is also limited to existing customers since November 2025.
o.D: CloudFront still charges internet data transfer, and one site downloading each object once gains nothing from caching.
